title: Physics I - Newton's Laws of Motion

learning_outcomes.statement: Distinguish velocity from acceleration and apply Newton's first law.
Compute acceleration from the vector sum of external forces and mass.
Identify Newton's third-law force pairs on different interacting bodies.
Construct a free-body diagram with only forces acting on the chosen body.
Reason about static and kinetic friction without assuming friction has a fixed value.
Explain reasoning to peers and apply a principle to a new situation.

misconceptions.MOTION_NEEDS_FORCE: Believes a continuing net force is required to sustain constant velocity.
misconceptions.FORCE_CAUSES_SPEED: Confuses force with speed rather than acceleration.
misconceptions.NET_VS_APPLIED: Uses an applied force instead of net external force.
misconceptions.MASS_ACCEL: Assumes a more massive body accelerates more under equal net force.
misconceptions.FBD_PAIR: Places action-reaction forces on the same free-body diagram.
misconceptions.THIRD_LAW_UNEQUAL: Believes the more massive/stronger body exerts a larger interaction force.
misconceptions.VELOCITY_FORCE: Infers a nonzero net force from nonzero constant velocity.
misconceptions.STATIC_FRICTION_ZERO: Assumes friction acts only once motion begins.
misconceptions.STATIC_FRICTION_MAX: Assumes static friction always equals its maximum available value.
misconceptions.FRICTION_WITH_MOTION: Misidentifies friction direction as necessarily the direction of velocity.
misconceptions.INCLINE_COMPONENT: Interchanges sine and cosine for weight components on incline.
misconceptions.SYSTEM_BOUNDARY: Cannot distinguish interaction forces when isolating a body versus a system.
